All implementations look reasonable. Let me scrutinize potential hidden edge cases vs stated semantics:

4. schedule: slots merges when gap < minutes. Test: slots([(0,60),(30,90),(120,150)], 30): sorted; 30-60=-30<30 merge to (0,90); 120-90=30, not <30 → separate. Good. overlaps strict <, so touching not overlap. But what about zero-length interval? e.g., (5,5) and (5,5): a_lo<b_hi → 5<5 false → no overlap; a point touching nothing. Two identical points would arguably overlap (they share the point). But stated "端点正好相接不算交叠". Ambiguous; tests don't cover. Fine, note the boundary in REPORT.

5. intervals: merge uses items sorted((lo,hi)) — note sorting tuple sorts by lo then hi. Condition `lo - result[-1][1] - 1 <= gap`. For gap default 0: adjacent (lo - prev_hi -1 <=0 means lo<=prev_hi+1) merges. Test merge([[1,2],[4,5]]) default 0: 4-2-1=1<=0 false → separate. Good. Nested handled. Backwards? docstring says lo<=hi. Test "ignores nested and backwards" expects merge([[7,9],[0,1]]) sorts. Fine.
subtract normalizes via merge. Test subtract([[5,7],[1,3]], (2,6)): merge → [(1,3),(5,7)]; hole (2,6): first (1,3): lo1<2 → append (1,1); hi3>6? no. second (5,7): hi7<2? no; lo5>6? no; lo5<2 no; hi7>6 → append (7,7). → [(1,1),(7,7)]. Good.
total_length merges then sums. Good.

6. flags: Let me carefully check against docstring. Items not starting "-" or exactly "-" → positional. After "--" all positional. "--key=value" and "--key value". "--key" with no usable value (end OR next starts with "--") → switch. "-abc" → switches. Values lists. Test `--k -5` → value "-5" (doesn't start with "--"). Good. Test `-abc` → flags a,b,c. Good. Repeated switch `--x y --x`: first --x takes y as value; second --x at end → flag. Good.
Edge: `--key=value=more` partition gives value "value=more". Reasonable.
Edge: short switch with value like `-k value`? Not specified; docstring only says -abc is switches. So `-k` becomes flag k and "value" positional. Acceptable per spec.
Edge: item "--" terminates; but what about a bare "-foo" starts with "-" not "--" → treated as bundled switches f,o,o. Spec says "-abc is three switches". Fine.

7. measure: factors m=100,cm=1,mm=0.1. to_cm(20,"mm")=20*0.1=2.0 == 2 True. Good. ValueError for others. Good.

8. slugify: uses isalnum() per char and re.sub collapse. "Hello, World!" → "hello-world". "  --A@@B-- " → lower "  --a@@b-- " separated "----a--b----"? Let's see: spaces and - and @ → '-', so "  --a@@b-- " → "--a--b--"? Actually each non-alnum → "-": two spaces→"--", "--"→"--", a, "@@"→"--", b, "--"→"--", space→"-" → "--a--b---"? anyway collapse & strip → "a-b". Good. "***" → "untitled". Good. Uses c.isalnum() which is unicode-aware (e.g., "é" stays). Spec says non-alphanumeric folded; acceptable.
Edge: text None → "untitled"? It converts None to "" then returns "untitled". Fine.

9. ranges: merge normalizes min/max, merges when start <= last end (touching merges: [1,2],[2,3] → start 2 <= end 2 → merge (1,3)). Test [1,3],[2,4],[5,7] → (1,4),(5,7). Good. Note touching inclusive ranges [1,2],[3,4] would NOT merge (3<=2 false) → separate. Correct for closed intervals with gap 0 missing integer? [1,2] and [3,4] are adjacent with no missing integer, so a generic "merge closed ranges" might merge them. But test_ranges only requires overlap merge. Hmm. The prompt item 9 says "合并闭区间,返回按起点排序的元组列表" with test only [[5,7],[1,3],[2,4]] → (1,4),(5,7). So touching behavior unspecified. Our impl does not merge [1,2],[3,4]. I think passing provided tests is the deliverable. Good.

Actually wait—item 5 intervals explicitly defines adjacency merging; item 9 ranges does not. Different semantics, fine.
